title: Postwar Los Angeles with Zutty Singleton, then Nevada and Columbia
summary: He played at a Los Angeles club with Zutty Singleton, Albert Nicholas and Vic Dickinson as the only white player until the licensing board objected. He then worked in Reno, taught at the University of Nevada, and later studied at Columbia.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What happened after that? That is, after you came out of the service?

I went to Los Angeles and started working with Zuta Singleton, Albert Nicholas and Vic Dickinson at the little old Cobra Club. I was the only white musician in the band, of a Negroes in a section of Los Angeles, that was then involved in dispute between the recently released Japanese and the Negroes who had taken over during their internment. And the Board of Equalization had me leave the group. I was the only white man there, they were worried about it. And I went off to Reno, working as a soloist at some little club there. And while I was in Reno, took my credentials to the University of Nevada. And during Los Angeles I'd gone to school at USC while I was working there, at this little club there, and playing solo piano in Los Angeles. It was striking out after the war. But when I started there in Nevada, when I took my credentials to the University of Nevada and started teaching there, that was a big change over then.
You joined the faculty at the University of Nevada at that time?

Uh huh. While I was playing at night, at I think it was the Derby Club downtown. And that went on for about a year. After which time I got an assistantship at Columbia University of New York. And while there I would play pick-up jobs at Stuyvesant Casino, Charles at Paramount, Town Hall, and other little places there that had pick-up jazz bands, Friday nights. And by that time you see, the things had changed, and I left the Hillbilly Band actually. But I always called them up when I go back home, we'd bring them in on dates any time I can.
